readme: THE ALERT REGISTRY (Brad, ruling 1, 2026-09-10; design/PLAN-zero-alert-days-2026-09-10.md section 7). Every alert type is exactly one class. page = emailed AND queued, for four conditions only: (1) the live board or feed is wrong or held, (2) a guard or watcher cannot see, (3) scheduled work did not run or did not land, (4) a live cell moved in a way automatic adjudication could not explain; escalations to Brad (send-alert -Escalates, Your call asks) are page too. review = queued for triage, NEVER emailed (triage-created residuals and findings, send-alert -Lane weekly, are review). digest = emailed, NEVER queued. send-alert.ps1 resolves the class through grocery/alert-registry-lib.ps1. An alert whose type matches NO entry is never dropped: it queues with unregistered=true AND is emailed with its subject prefixed 'UNREGISTERED ALERT TYPE: '. A registry that is missing or unparseable makes EVERY alert page. MATCHING: send-alert derives a type key from the subject (lower case, dates, rc=N and every number removed, every run of non-letters collapsed to one space); 'key' is compared to that type key. match 'exact' = equal; 'prefix' = the type key starts with key at a word boundary; 'regex' = .NET regex over the type key. When several entries match, exact beats prefix and regex; several that still tie are AMBIGUOUS and resolve to the most severe class. TO ADD A TYPE: add one entry here (id, match, key, class, condition, emitter), then run powershell -File grocery/audit-alert-registry.ps1, which must exit 0. condition for page is one of the five values in page_conditions; for review and digest it is one line saying why.
